mainTopic: Blood in a piece of tissue, קרי drawn out with a splinter and a זב's count, and whether dry blood makes a woman a נדה
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the argument about blood found inside a piece of tissue (חתיכה). The first explanation says the argument is about whether women normally see blood this way. רבא disagrees: everyone agrees women do not, and the real argument is whether the blood can be impure because it passed through the מקור even though the woman stays pure. Next, רבה asks רב הונא whether a man is impure from קרי drawn out with a splinter. רב הונא answers that קרי only makes impure in an amount that blocks the opening. A long back-and-forth follows about why a זב's קרי breaks his seven clean days, and why it breaks only one day. Finally, רבי יוסי בר' חנינא asks רבי אלעזר whether blood that comes out dry makes a woman a נדה. רבי אלעזר starts a proof from our משנה about a woman who discharges odd red items, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The argument is about blood inside a piece of tissue
steps.stepSummary: The two sides argue about whether a woman normally sees menstrual blood inside a discharged piece of tissue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is about a piece of tissue. One side holds that women normally see blood in a piece of tissue. The other side holds that women do not normally see blood in a piece of tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly where the two opinions in the ברייתא disagree. The argument is about blood found inside a piece of tissue (חתיכה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If women normally see menstrual blood this way, then blood inside the tissue counts as real menstrual blood, and she becomes impure. If women do not normally see blood this way, then this blood is not her menstrual blood, and she stays pure. So the whole argument depends on what is 'normal' for a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they disagree (this marks the exact point of the argument)
A piece of tissue that a woman discharges
The normal way of a woman

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is about a piece of tissue.
phrases.notes: He means blood found inside the cracks of a piece of tissue that the woman discharged.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: it is the normal way of a woman
to see blood in a piece of tissue,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין דַּרְכָּהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: it is not the normal way of a woman
to see blood in a piece of tissue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an explanation of the ברייתא's argument that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument depends on whether women normally see menstrual blood inside a piece of tissue.

steps.title: רבא: everyone agrees women do not normally see blood in tissue
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the first explanation and says both sides agree that women do not normally see blood in a piece of tissue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Everyone agrees that women do not normally see blood in a piece of tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different way to understand the argument. He starts by removing the point the first explanation depended on, and his next line will give the real point of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first explanation said the two sides argue about what is normal for a woman. רבא says there is no argument about that: both sides agree it is not normal. So he must find a different reason they disagree, which he gives in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (both sides hold this)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not adding to the first explanation. He is replacing it with a different explanation of the same argument.

phrases.english: Rava says: Everyone agrees
that it is not the normal way of a woman
to see blood in a piece of tissue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea behind step 1 and begins a different explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree that women do not normally see menstrual blood in a piece of tissue.

steps.title: The real argument: can the woman be pure while the blood is impure?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, רבי אליעזר holds the woman is pure but the blood is impure because it passed through the מקור. רבנן hold that the מקור is pure here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they argue about whether a woman can be pure while the place of the מקור is impure. רבי אליעזר holds: the woman is pure, but the blood is impure, because it came through the מקור. רבנן hold: the woman is pure, and the place of the מקור is also pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives the real point of the argument. Both sides agree the woman herself is not a נדה, but they argue about whether the blood is still impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says the blood is impure because it passed through the מקור, which is an impure place, even though the woman herself did not become a נדה. רבנן say that in this case the מקור is also pure, so the blood is not impure either. The question is no longer 'what is normal' but 'can the passage be impure while the woman is pure?'

keyTerms.meaning: The source, meaning the womb, where menstrual blood comes from
They disagree
The woman is pure (she is not a נדה)
The blood is impure

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, both sides agree the woman is not a נדה. רבי אליעזר still calls the blood impure because it passed through the מקור, while רבנן say the מקור is pure here and so is the blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the woman's status and the blood's status can be separate questions. The woman can be pure while something that came out of her is still impure.

phrases.english: And here, about a woman who is pure
while the place of the source is impure, they disagree,
phrases.notes: Here 'source' (מקור) means the womb, where menstrual blood comes from.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Eliezer holds:
the woman is pure, but the blood is impure,
because it came through the source,
and the Rabbis hold: the woman is pure,
and the place of the source is also pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא, בְּאִשָּׁה טְהוֹרָה וּמְקוֹר מְקוֹמוֹ טָמֵא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's explanation by giving the real point of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the woman is pure but the blood is impure because it passed through the מקור. רבנן: the woman and the מקור are both pure.

steps.title: רבה asks: is קרי drawn out with a splinter impure?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks רב הונא whether a man becomes impure when קרי is drawn out with a splinter of wood, and explains both possible readings of the word ממנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked רב הונא: If a man sees קרי by drawing it out with a splinter of wood, what is the law? The Torah says 'from him' — does that mean it must come out of his body by itself, and not with a splinter? Or does 'from him' only mean his impurity must come outside, so even with a splinter he is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבה asks רב הונא whether a man is impure when his קרי comes out because it was drawn out with a splinter, not on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question depends on how to read the word 'ממנו' (from him) in the פסוק. One reading says it must come from his own body by itself, so a splinter does not count. The other reading says it only needs to come outside his body, so a splinter does count. רב הונא answers in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission, which makes a man impure
A splinter or thin stick of wood
What is the law?
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
From him (the key word in the פסוק)
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the קרי came out. The question is only whether coming out with help from a splinter counts the same as coming out on its own.

phrases.english: Rabba asked Rav Huna:
One who sees semen with a splinter of wood, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the man drew the semen out with the splinter, so it did not come out on its own.

phrases.english: The Torah said 'from him' —
so it must come out of his flesh by itself, and not with a splinter,
or perhaps this 'from him' means —
only that his impurity must come outside,
phrases.notes: 'His impurity' here is the semen itself.

phrases.english: so even with a splinter it also counts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a question about a man's impurity from קרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a man become impure from קרי that was drawn out with a splinter of wood, or must it come out of his body by itself?

steps.title: רב הונא: קרי only makes impure when there is enough to block the opening
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the man is pure, because קרי only makes impure in an amount large enough to block the opening of the organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You can work it out from the fact that the קרי itself only makes a person impure when there is enough of it to block the opening of the organ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רבה's question from the previous step. He says there is no need to decide how to read ממנו, because the man is pure for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרי only makes impure if there is a minimum amount, enough to block the opening of the organ. A splinter cannot draw out that much, so the man stays pure no matter how we read the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Derive it instead from (a simpler reason)
Blocking of the opening of the organ: the minimum amount of קרי that makes impure
Makes impure

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב הונא is answering רבה's question from the last step.

phrases.english: Derive it from the fact that it itself
does not make impure except
when there is enough to block the opening of the organ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבה's question about קרי drawn out with a splinter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קרי pulled out with a splinter makes the man impure.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, because קרי only makes impure in an amount that blocks the opening, and a splinter cannot draw that much.

steps.title: If impurity comes from touching, why does קרי break a זב's count?
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that a size requirement means the impurity comes from touching the קרי. That clashes with a ברייתא that says קרי breaks the seven clean days of a זב, just as זיבה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say he is impure as someone who touches it? But if so, קרי should not break the count of a זב! Why, then, is it taught: 'This is the law of the זב, and of one from whom semen goes out.' Just as זיבה breaks the count, so too קרי breaks the count?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges רב הונא's answer. He backs up the challenge with a ברייתא about the seven clean days of a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an amount is needed, then the man's impurity is not from the emission itself. It comes from his body touching the קרי, like a נוגע. Touching impurity does not break a זב's seven clean days. But the ברייתא learns from the פסוק that קרי does break them, just like זיבה, so it must be the emission itself that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: One who touches: someone who is impure because of contact, not because of something coming out of him
But if so: introduces an unacceptable result of the idea being challenged
Breaks (cancels) the count of the seven clean days
The discharge that makes a man a זב
Semen, also called קרי

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the man is impure from קרי. It is about why he is impure: from the emission itself, or from touching the קרי. That difference decides whether it can break a זב's count.

phrases.english: Is this to say that he is one who touches?
phrases.notes: Since there is a size requirement, it sounds like he is impure only because his body touches the קרי.

phrases.english: But if so,
it should not break the count in זיבה!
phrases.notes: A זב must count seven clean days, and simply touching something impure doesn't cancel them.

phrases.english: Why, then, is it taught:
"This is the law of the זב
and of one from whom semen goes out"
just as זיבה breaks the count,
so too semen also breaks the count?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logical result of רב הונא's size-requirement answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that קרי only makes impure in a blocking amount.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A size requirement implies impurity by touching. Touching does not break a זב's count, yet the ברייתא says קרי does.

steps.title: קרי breaks the count only because it always contains bits of זיבה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that קרי breaks a זב's count not because of the emission itself. It breaks it because a זב's קרי always has tiny bits of זיבה mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Breaking the count — this is the reason it breaks it: because it is impossible for it to come without bits of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his answer by giving a different reason why קרי breaks a זב's seven clean days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not prove that קרי's emission itself makes impure. A זב's קרי always carries traces of זיבה, and the זיבה is what breaks the count. So רב הונא can still say the impurity of קרי comes from touching and needs a minimum amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiny drops or traces of זיבה
This is the reason

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: קרי needs a blocking amount to make impure, so a splinter does not make the man impure. קרי breaks a זב's count only because it always contains traces of זיבה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Breaking the count —
this is the reason it breaks it:
because it is impossible for it
without bits of זיבה.
phrases.notes: He means a זב's קרי always has a little זיבה mixed in, and that זיבה is what cancels the count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְתִירָה הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּסוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the reason behind the ברייתא's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קרי breaks a זב's count because its emission itself makes impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: It breaks the count only because a זב's קרי always contains bits of זיבה.

steps.title: If the problem is mixed-in זיבה, it should break all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב הונא's answer from Step 7. If קרי breaks the count only because of the זיבה mixed into it, it should break all seven days like real זיבה. But a ברייתא says it breaks only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, the קרי should break all seven days! Why, then, does a ברייתא teach: 'This is the law of the זב, etc.' Just as זיבה breaks the count, so does semen. You might think that just as זיבה breaks all seven days, semen also breaks all seven. So the verse says 'to be impure by it': it has only what is stated about it, so it breaks just one day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב הונא's last answer. He says it leads to a result that a ברייתא clearly rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב must count seven clean days. Seeing זיבה during those days cancels the whole count, and he starts over. רב הונא said a זב's קרי breaks the count because it contains bits of זיבה. רבה argues that this logic should make it cancel all seven days, yet the ברייתא learns from the verse that קרי cancels only one day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If just as...': the ברייתא tests whether the comparison goes all the way
'The verse teaches': it introduces a verse that settles the question
All seven clean days of a זב's count

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'breaking the count' with 'making him impure.' The question here is how many of the seven clean days are lost: all seven, or only one.

phrases.english: But if so, it should break all seven days!
phrases.notes: "It" is the קרי. If it really carries זיבה, it should act like זיבה.

phrases.english: Why, then, is it taught:
"This is the law of the זב, etc."
Just as זיבה breaks the count,
so too, semen breaks the count.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה זִיבָה סוֹתֶרֶת כׇּל שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.english: If so, then just as זיבה breaks all seven days,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע נָמֵי סוֹתֶרֶת כׇּל שִׁבְעָה?
phrases.english: should semen also break all seven days?
The verse says: "to be impure by it"
phrases.notes: These words come from the same verse. They describe the קרי, which makes a person impure for one day.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ בָּהּ אֶלָּא מָה שֶׁאָמוּר בָּהּ,
phrases.english: you have in it only what is stated about it,
so it breaks only one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, תִּסְתּוֹר כׇּל שִׁבְעָה? אַלְּמָה תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer רב הונא gave in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that a זב's קרי breaks the count because of mixed-in זיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the זיבה inside is what breaks the count, the full seven days should be lost. Yet the ברייתא limits it to one day.

steps.title: A Torah decree: pure זיבה breaks seven, mixed bits break one
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the Torah itself decided this. Pure זיבה breaks all seven days, while small bits of זיבה mixed with semen break only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a decree of the verse. Complete זיבה, with no semen mixed in, breaks all seven days. Bits of זיבה with semen mixed in break only one day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his position against רבה's challenge. He explains that the Torah simply gave mixed זיבה a smaller effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא keeps his reason: the קרי breaks the count because of the זיבה inside it. He explains the one-day limit as a גזירת הכתוב. When the זיבה is only small bits mixed with semen, the Torah treats it more lightly than pure זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree of the verse, a rule the Torah sets without a stated logical reason
Complete, pure זיבה
Mixed in

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, a זב's קרי breaks his count because of the bits of זיבה inside it, but the Torah limits the loss to one day.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a decree of the verse.

phrases.aramaic: זִיבָה גְּמוּרָה דְּלָא עֲרִבָה בַּהּ שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע
phrases.english: Complete זיבה, with no semen mixed in,
breaks all seven days.

phrases.aramaic: צִחְצוּחֵי זִיבָה דַּעֲרִבָה בַּהּ שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע
phrases.english: Bits of זיבה with semen mixed in
break only one day.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Torah decree (גזירת הכתוב) distinguishing two kinds of זיבה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any זיבה, even small bits mixed with semen, should break all seven days
steps.terutzMaskana: Only pure זיבה breaks seven days. Bits of זיבה mixed with semen break one day, by Torah decree.

steps.title: Does dry blood make a woman impure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר' חנינא asks רבי אלעזר whether dry blood makes a woman a נדה. Maybe the verse 'if her blood flows' means only wet blood counts. Or maybe the verse just describes the usual way blood comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא asked רבי אלעזר: What is the law with dry blood? The Torah says 'if her blood flows,' so maybe she is impure only when it flows: wet, yes; dry, no. Or perhaps 'if her blood flows' just describes the normal way things happen, and really even dry blood makes her impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks whether blood that comes out dry makes a woman impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question depends on how to read the word 'flows' in the verse. One reading makes 'flowing' a real requirement, so only wet blood counts. The other reading says the verse just describes the usual case, so dry blood counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: Dry blood
Wet, moist
'If her blood flows': the words of the פסוק the question is about
The normal way things happen. The verse describes the usual case and is not setting a requirement.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מֵרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, asked Rabbi Elazar:
What is the law with dry blood?
The Merciful One said: "If her blood flows"
so maybe she is impure only once the blood actually flows:
wet, yes; dry, no.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: הַאי ״כִּי יָזוּב זָב דָּמָה״
phrases.english: Or perhaps this phrase, "if her blood flows,"
just describes the normal way it happens,
and really, even dry blood also makes her impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מֵרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: דָּם יָבֵשׁ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the זב discussion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether dry blood makes a woman a נדה, or whether the verse requires the blood to flow

steps.title: First answer: נדה blood is impure wet or dry
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that a משנה already teaches that דם הנדה makes things impure whether it is wet or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this in a משנה: The blood of a נדה and the flesh of a dead body make things impure whether they are wet or dry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question from Step 10. He points to a משנה that says נדה blood is impure even when it is dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether dry blood counts as נדה blood. רבי אלעזר's answer is simple: a משנה says דם הנדה makes things impure even when dry. So he says dry blood clearly counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of a woman who is a נדה
The flesh of a dead body
They make things impure
Wet and dry

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it already:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר is speaking. He means the answer is already in a משנה.

phrases.english: The blood of a נדה and the flesh of a dead body
make things impure, whether wet or dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether dry blood makes a woman a נדה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. A משנה states that נדה blood makes things impure whether it is wet or dry.

steps.title: The question is about blood that was dry from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר' חנינא says the משנה only covers blood that came out wet and later dried. His real question is about blood that was already dry when it came out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am not asking about blood that was wet and then became dry. What I am asking about is blood that was dry from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר' חנינא rejects the proof from Step 11. He explains exactly which case he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה can be read as talking about blood that left the body wet and then dried. That blood already became impure while it was wet, so drying does not help. The question is about blood that came out dry, which might never have counted as 'flowing' blood as the verse says.

keyTerms.meaning: Wet and then became dry
Dry from the very beginning
I am not asking about this
What I am really asking about

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי בר' חנינא disagrees with the משנה. He accepts it fully. He is only saying it talks about a different case than his question.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רבי יוסי בר' חנינא is answering רבי אלעזר.

phrases.aramaic: לַח וְנַעֲשָׂה יָבֵשׁ — לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: Blood that was wet and became dry, I am not asking about;
what I am asking about is blood that was dry from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַח וְנַעֲשָׂה יָבֵשׁ — לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 11 by limiting the משנה to a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה of 'wet or dry' is rejected for this question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That משנה can be talking about blood that left the body wet and only dried later, not blood that was dry when it came out.

steps.title: Second proof: the woman who discharges odd red items
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says this question is also answered by a משנה. It is the משנה about a woman who discharges something like a shell, hair, soil or red gnats, which she must put in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too you learned: A woman who discharges something like a shell, like a hair, like soil, or like red gnats should put it into water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a second source to answer the narrower question. The text quotes the start of the משנה here, and the proof from it finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items in this משנה come out dry and solid, not as flowing blood. Since the משנה says to test them in water, it seems to treat dry blood as something that could make her a נדה. The rest of the משנה and the exact proof come next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 12 narrowed the question to blood that was dry from the start, רבי אלעזר brings a new source aimed at exactly that case.
steps.raayaObject: That blood which is dry from the very start can make a woman a נדה.
